---
title: "ESS and WID Descriptive Analysis"
format: html
---

This report compares country-year summaries of satisfaction with the state of
the economy (ESS `stfeco`) with distributional series from the World Inequality
Database (WID). Only years available in ESS and in both WID concepts are plotted
for a country.



## Data Validity

An observation is valid for comparison only when ESS flags the country-year as
reliable, both WID distributions contain all ten equal-split adult decile shares
and sum to one within 2.5 percentage points, and neither WID series marks the
year as extrapolated. The WID metadata does not identify all interpolated years.
Observations failing any rule are excluded from every section after
comparability.


::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output-display}


|Validity check                | Passing country-years| Matched country-years|
|:-----------------------------|---------------------:|---------------------:|
|ESS reliable                  |                   267|                   369|
|Complete valid wealth deciles |                   369|                   369|
|Wealth not extrapolated       |                   369|                   369|
|Complete valid income deciles |                   369|                   369|
|Income not extrapolated       |                   307|                   369|
|Pass all validity checks      |                   225|                   369|


:::
:::

## Descriptive ESS-WID Association

The merged table uses the earliest matched observation in each two-year ESS
round and the corresponding WID distribution. It retains ESS reliability,
effective sample size, the selected post-tax income series where available,
and WID extrapolation flags. The full country-round table is available as
[data/processed/ess_wid_country_round.csv](data/processed/ess_wid_country_round.csv).

All summaries and correlations below use ESS observations flagged reliable.
Correlations are descriptive only; no significance tests are performed. The
Gini values are approximated from WID's ten decile shares. Negative net wealth
shares can produce wealth Gini values above one.

Between-country and within-country percentages describe where the reliable

## WID Distribution Change

This section summarizes annualized distribution changes for WID countries that
also have ESS country-year data. Years are grouped into two-year ESS rounds
anchored at 2002; the earliest matched observation in each round is used. Each
reported transition compares consecutive selected ESS observations, skipping
intervening WID years. WID post-tax national-income shares are used where
available, with pre-tax shares as a fallback. For each transition, the score is
the mean absolute change across the nine cumulative decile-share cutoffs,
divided by the gap between ESS observations. It is a magnitude in percentage
points per year; it does not indicate whether inequality rose or fell. The
metric uses the cumulative share profile directly, so it also applies when net
wealth shares are negative.

### Wealth and Income Change by Country

Each point is a country, positioned by its median annualized change for wealth
and income. Larger values mean more movement in the cumulative share profile;
no direction is implied.


::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![](figures/descriptive/distribution_change/wid/country_comparison.png){width=700}
:::
:::


### Largest WID Country-Year Changes

The top transitions are ranked by annualized magnitude and use consecutive ESS
observation years as endpoints. An asterisk indicates that one endpoint falls
within a WID metadata-declared extrapolation interval.


::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![](figures/descriptive/distribution_change/wid/largest_changes.png){width=900}
:::
:::



## ESS Summary Change

ESS changes are calculated independently of WID. The mean measures movement in
average satisfaction with the state of the economy; the IQR measures change in
spread. Both are annualized absolute changes in ESS scale points. Years are
grouped into two-year ESS rounds anchored at 2002, using the earliest available
observation in each round. Heatmap columns label the selected endpoint pairs.
Unreliable or unknown endpoints appear as blank cells.

### Largest ESS Mean and IQR Changes

The largest mean changes are ranked by annualized magnitude. The IQR panel shows
the observed IQR at both ESS endpoints for the largest annualized IQR changes,
making the before/after spread visible. Segment color indicates whether the IQR
widened or narrowed; an asterisk marks an unreliable or unclassified endpoint.


::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![](figures/descriptive/distribution_change/ess/largest_changes.png){width=950}
:::
:::
